items.title: Now available: Depot Wrapped 2025
items.summary: Get a recap of your 2025 usage of Depot with our brand new Depot Wrapped. Check out your usage and grab an easter egg for an upcoming Depot launch.

items.title: How support shapes the product at Depot
items.summary: Learn how support shapes the product at Depot and how we've improved our self-service support experience.

items.title: Introducing Sherlock: AI assistant for Depot docs
items.summary: We built Sherlock, an AI assistant for the Depot docs. Sherlock searches our documentation with direct access to the markdown source, so answers come exclusively from our content with links to the docs it referenced. We also think Sherlock is outrageously cute.

items.title: Graceful Shutdown in Go
items.summary: When graceful shutdown is an afterthought, it's one of the most common sources of production bugs. When servers restart, work gets dropped, state gets lost, and you end up chasing weird behavior at startup. Here's how to use contexts and WaitGroups to implement clean shutdowns that don't lose work or corrupt state.

items.title: The ultimate guide to Docker build cache
items.summary: Ever wondered when Docker reuses cached layers and when it rebuilds from scratch? This guide breaks down the mechanics of how caching works, how cache invalidation cascades through your builds, and how different instructions affect the cache.

items.title: Scaling Depot: Solving a thundering herd problem
items.summary: When upstream systems fail, retries pile up fast and your database becomes the bottleneck. Here's how we used PlanetScale's Insights to identify and fix the queries that were slowing us down during thundering herd events.

items.title: Now available: GitHub Actions analytics
items.summary: We're launching GitHub Actions analytics in Depot. Make informed decisions about your workflows, with performance trends, resource utilization, and optimization recommendations across all GitHub Actions jobs.

items.title: Troubleshooting GitHub Actions with self-hosted runners
items.summary: Not every self-hosted runner failure is actually a runner problem. GitHub Actions and third-party actions often expect environmental features that GitHub-hosted runners provide by default. When your setup differs, you may get cryptic errors that point to the wrong cause. Here are three real support cases where the symptoms looked like runner issues but weren't.

items.title: We hire people who care about their work
items.summary: There is a ton of slop out in the world nowadays. If you want to stand out from the crowd, think about quality and giving a shit about people and problems.

items.title: Knowledge share: Insights from the us-east-1 outage on October 20th
items.summary: We were affected by the major us-east-1 outage on October 20th that disrupted several core AWS services. Here is how we were impacted, how we responded, and what we're doing to make our system more resilient to full region outages in the future.

items.title: Now available: Github Actions log search
items.summary: We're launching GitHub Actions log search in Depot. Search across all your historical CI logs with powerful keyword search and filtering capabilities.

items.title: How BuildKit Parallelizes Your Builds
items.summary: BuildKit's DAG solver transforms your Dockerfile into an optimized execution plan, finding every opportunity to run things in parallel. Learn how stage parallelism, instruction parallelism, and work deduplication combine to dramatically speed up your container builds.

items.title: A marketer's hour of hell: What I finally get about slow builds
items.summary: I thought I understood slow builds until I broke our docs and spent an hour fixing what should've taken 10 minutes. That's when I finally got it.

items.title: What technical writers actually do at startups
items.summary: Technical writers at startups touch every part of the organization, building relationships across engineering, support, and marketing to shape how the company thinks about content from the ground up.

items.title: Why 98.5% of organizations have slow actions/checkout
items.summary: We analyzed over 60,000 checkout steps in GitHub Actions runners. 98.5% of organizations could be missing out on massive performance gains.

items.title: Node 20 deprecation: PSA for Depot users
items.summary: GitHub is deprecating Node.js 20 for authoring GitHub Actions. Here's what you need to know.

items.title: We analyzed 66,821 GitHub Actions runs: 9 hidden gems you're missing
items.summary: We analyzed 66,821 GitHub Actions workflow runs to uncover valuable third-party actions that teams are using to speed up CI pipelines and improve developer productivity. The data reveals hidden gems in the Actions marketplace that could transform your workflows.

items.title: Collaborating with Claude on docs
items.summary: Experiments with using Claude in Depot remote sandboxes to identify documentation gaps, generate drafts, and collaborate with your team on keeping docs up to date.

items.title: Git is really cool, actually
items.summary: Git's fetch operation shows off the best of its design: simple request-response exchanges and packfiles that sync repos efficiently. Here's how it works and why modern development needs more.

items.title: Using AI as my engineering copilot (not autopilot)
items.summary: AI has become incredibly powerful for engineering work, but treating it as an autopilot without providing a ton of context can lead to messy, unmaintainable code. Here's how I use AI as a copilot instead to accelerate my work while keeping control over architecture, patterns, and code quality.

items.title: From Go code to container image with Depot API
items.summary: Build a specialized container building system using Depot's low-level Go SDK to transform tar archives into container images. This advanced walkthrough demonstrates the three-step build flow: registering builds, acquiring ephemeral BuildKit machines, and configuring custom build solutions.

items.title: Monorepos: Worth the hype?
items.summary: Monorepos promise faster development and better visibility across your stack. But they also introduce scaling problems most teams do not see coming. This post breaks down the tradeoffs, the tooling challenges, and when a monorepo actually makes sense.

items.title: GitHub Actions Runner architecture: The listener
items.summary: GitHub Actions Runners power every job you run, whether on GitHub-hosted machines or your own hardware. But the way they work and the APIs they talk to have been changing. In this first part of our deep dive, we unpack the Listener process, how it's evolved from Azure DevOps roots, and what those changes mean for anyone running or accelerating Actions with Depot.

items.title: Now available: Remote agent sandboxes on Depot
items.summary: We've brought remote agent sandboxes to Depot, starting with remote Claude Code agents. Run AI coding sessions in persistent cloud sandboxes with full filesystem context, Git integration, and session sharing across your entire team. No more starting from scratch in async environments.

items.title: The hidden cost of self hosting CI runners
items.summary: Self hosting CI runners sounds great. You get control, flexibility, and the promise of lower cost. But most teams that try it end up burned out and buried in maintenance. Between flaky APIs, surprise cloud bills, and endless patching, the tradeoffs add up fast. Here's what actually happens when you go it alone and why some teams decide not to.

items.title: Guide to faster Rust builds in CI
items.summary: Building Rust projects in CI can be painfully slow, but with the right optimizations, you can dramatically reduce build times. We tested various techniques on the Zed codebase and achieved a 35% speedup over our already-optimized baseline, cutting build times from 27 minutes to just 16 minutes.

items.title: A practical guide to debugging GitHub Actions
items.summary: GitHub Actions are great when they just work, but a single failing job can bring everything to a halt. Sometimes the error is obvious, other times it feels like the runner is failing for reasons that have nothing to do with your code. This guide walks through practical ways to debug those failures so you can get builds running smoothly again.

items.title: How we automated GitHub Actions Runner updates with Claude
items.summary: Maintaining forks of rapidly-evolving upstream repositories is a productivity killer. At Depot, we were spending hours each week manually updating ARM64 patches and reviewing dozens of commits just to keep our GitHub Actions runner images in sync. Here's how we used Claude Code to automate the entire process, turning a weekly time sink into a hands-off CI workflow.

items.title: How to use cache mounts to speed up Docker builds
items.summary: Cache mounts let you preserve partial build state between Docker builds, making incremental rebuilds faster when layer cache misses. Here's how to use them effectively, avoid common pitfalls, and make them work reliably in CI environments.

items.title: Introducing GitHub Job Details: Observability for your CI/CD pipeline
items.summary: GitHub Job Details are now live in the Depot app. See exactly how your GitHub Actions workflows performed with detailed visibility into job execution, resource usage, and debugging data all in one place.

items.title: Now available: Build autoscaling for everyone
items.summary: We're excited to roll out the general availability of container build autoscaling for all container build projects in Depot. This feature allows you to automatically scale out your container builds to multiple BuildKit builders based on how many concurrent builds you want processing on a single builder.

items.title: Now available: Claude Code sessions in Depot
items.summary: We're excited to launch Claude Code sessions in Depot. This enables seamless collaboration between AI coding agents and your team by allowing anyone in your organization to pick up and resume Claude sessions.

items.title: How to reduce CI/CD costs: Complete optimization checklist
items.summary: Most engineering teams overspend on CI/CD by 50% or more. Here's how to cut your build costs in half without slowing down deployments.

items.title: Container security at scale: Building untrusted images safely
items.summary: Many SaaS platforms need to run customer code securely and fast. Rather than building container infrastructure from scratch, you can use Depot's API to handle the heavy lifting. Here's how to build Go tooling that creates isolated projects, manages builds, and tracks metrics for your customer workloads.

items.title: DevOps to finance: Explaining CI costs to your CFO
items.summary: Why did our CI costs spike 40% this quarter?" It's the dreaded question that makes every DevOps engineer's heart sink. This post will help you translate technical realities into financial terms, positioning yourself as a strategic partner instead of just another cost center asking for more budget.

items.title: Now available: Egress filtering for GitHub Actions Runners
items.summary: We're excited to launch egress filtering for Depot GitHub Actions Runners. This gives you fine-grained control over which external services your runners can talk to so you can tighten security without giving up performance or flexibility..

items.title: Now available: Windows GitHub Actions runners
items.summary: We're excited to announce that Windows GitHub Actions runners are now generally available across Depot for all pricing plans! Meaning you can now run all of your Windows builds with the performance of Depot at 4x cheaper than GitHub hosted runners.

items.title: Why platform teams are focused on CI/CD optimization
items.summary: New data shows 71% of platform engineering teams are prioritizing CI/CD optimization. Mid-sized orgs lead the charge, and for good reason, slow builds are still one of the biggest blockers to developer productivity.

items.title: How to calculate your real GitHub Actions usage in minutes
items.summary: GitHub Actions usage reporting doesn't tell the full story. If you're running different types of runners (like 4-core, 8-core, or more), those minutes aren't equal, and your total usage number doesn't reflect it.

items.title: Now available: Audit logging for improved security
items.summary: We're excited to announce the launch of Audit Logging in the Depot web app, a critical step forward for security and operational accountability. Audit logging gives you a clear, timestamped record of key actions that lets you track important changes and identify exactly who made them.

items.title: Now available: Gocache v2 for improved Golang build performance
items.summary: We’re excited to announce Gocache v2, a major step forward in build caching for Go developers. Gocache v2 dramatically reduces build times by efficiently bundling and caching compile and test artifacts, and it’s now available in Depot Cache.

items.title: Faster Claude Code agents in GitHub Actions
items.summary: A crash course into the new ability to run Claude Code agents in GitHub Actions and how to make them faster with Depot runners.

items.title: From Go Code to Container Image with Depot API
items.summary: The Depot API lets you build and push containers straight from your Go code. No Docker CLI. No scripts. Just fast, native builds triggered by a few lines of Go.

items.title: Accelerating builds: Improving EC2 boot time from 4s to 2.8s
items.summary: We at Depot like making shit fast, whether that's Docker image builds, Github Actions runners, Bazel caching, Turborepo, or even our own infrastructure. Recently, we've been working to make EC2 instances boot faster.

items.title: Knowledge share: Insights from our major outage on May 8th
items.summary: We had a major outage on May 8th that took our core provisioning system for builds offline for several hours. This was a major incident that disrupted thousands of builds across Depot. We wanted to share some insights into what happened, how we fixed it, and what we're doing to prevent it in the future.

items.title: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners aren't free
items.summary: Self-hosting GitHub Actions runners isn't the "set it and forget it" option that folks may think it is. In this post, we will dive into why that is the case, and what the hidden costs are.

items.title: Why you should avoid COPY --link in your Dockerfile
items.summary: Often touted as a method for decreasing Docker image build times, COPY --link is actually more likely to have the opposite effect. Here's why.

items.title: Now available: Connect Depot to your Tailscale tailnet
items.summary: We're excited to announce that Depot now integrates with Tailscale, enabling secure, identity-driven access to your devices, services, and cloud networks. Learn how to connect to your Tailscale tailnet with Depot.

items.title: How to reduce your Docker image size
items.summary: Leverage .dockerignore, smaller base images, cache mounts, and multi-stage builds to drastically reduce the size of your Docker images.

items.title: How to reuse builds across integration test workflows
items.summary: Learn how to build and store your integration test builds once, and then pull them for multiple workflows as needed.
